outcome: The first READER IMPLEMENTATION of the DD-29 capability registry: a fail-closed resolver (resolveCapability) in @plexco/db that reads plans.entitlements.capabilities[key] for a tenant's current plan and returns a cause-agnostic decision. The entitlements/capabilities jsonb has had 0 PRODUCTION readers since 2026-08-07 (test readers exist — migrate.test.ts asserts the DD-29 seed, capability.test.ts exercises this resolver); this provides the production reader but it remains CODE-DARK (zero production callers — index.ts re-exports it) until a separately-authorized production enforcement point wires it. Hard dependency for DD-114 (money features gate on host_pro).
_lineage: This slice is the DD-29 §4b COMMERCIAL plan-entitlement resolver ONLY: resolveCapability answers 'does this tenant's paid plan tier (free vs host_pro) include this feature flag', reading plans.entitlements.capabilities. Despite the shared word 'capability', that is a DIFFERENT concern from the DD-56 ACTOR-authorization authority. DD-56 (decisions.md:720 'Co-admin capability') and feature_tenant_routing_authz_tech.md define `tenant-capability-authority-core` as a SEPARATE, MANDATORY, still-UNIMPLEMENTED cross-feature prerequisite: a closed action->capability registry, least-privilege presets for admin|co_admin, a per-tenant/person role resolver, tenant-private grant storage with expiry/revocation, append-only grant audit, and a fail-closed authorize(action, actor, target) over new monotonic migrations. NONE of that is implemented by this slice or satisfied by migrations 0028/0029/0009 — 0028/0029 landed only the DD-29 commercial plan catalog + entitlements shape, and 0009 is the general RLS grant loop, neither is DD-56's actor-capability registry/grants/audit. This slice neither implements nor reduces the DD-56 authority core and makes no part of it optional; that authority remains a full, unimplemented deliverable. The historical backlog task `tenant-capability-authority-core` conflated the two 'capability' concepts; this slice extracts the DD-29 commercial resolver only (codex round-02 [P1]).

_scope_disposition: ONE cohesive slice, kept whole on purpose (scope is a ceiling, not a target; the invariants forbid over-splitting cohesive low-risk work). 3 code modules touched: capability.ts (resolver, ~90 non-comment LOC — the rest is docstring), capability.test.ts (the fail-closed + concurrency matrix, appropriately large for a P1 money/authz choke-point), and a one-line index.ts barrel export. The ~300-LOC ceiling governs production logic across ≤3 modules; the total insertion count is dominated by the test matrix and heavy documentation, which the ceiling does not target. Splitting a resolver from its own acceptance suite would be the exact over-split the scope invariant warns against, so this ships as one slice with the LOC disposition recorded explicitly (codex round-01 [P2]).
